$comment: Five regions, and the tone each one is drawn in when there is no photograph. The tone is a design decision recorded as data rather than typed into a stylesheet, and it is the reason a country without a picture still looks like somewhere: every unresolved slot is drawn on its own region's ground, so moving from the Sahel to the Cape changes the colour of the page even before a photograph exists. All five are cut from the Afrinkong palette — deep forest, burnt sienna and muted gold, taken down to grounds dark enough to carry ivory type at 7:1 or better and the metadata voice at 4.5:1. All five sit inside the palette — they are values of the same ink, not five new brand colours — and none of them claims anything about the place beyond what its own terrain words already say.

central.name: Central & West
central.line: Rainforest, volcanic coast, savanna, ancient kingdoms and the cultures of the Gulf of Guinea.
central.tone_note: Rainforest and volcanic ground: deep forest opened up a step, so a plate on the dark band is still a panel and not a hole in it.

east.name: East Africa
east.line: The Rift, the great migrations, the gorilla forests, Kilimanjaro, the Nile and the Swahili coast.
east.tone_note: The Rift in open green — the lightest of the three greens, for the region with the most sky in it.

southern.name: Southern Africa
southern.line: The Namib, the Zambezi, the Kalahari, the Cape, and wilderness you walk rather than drive.
southern.tone_note: Burnt sienna as earth rather than as ink: the desert south, and the warmest ground in the set.

north.name: North Africa
north.line: The Atlas, the Sahara, the Nile, and Mediterranean cities older than most countries.
north.tone_note: Muted gold as ground. The Sahara, and the only one of the five that is more yellow than red.

islands.name: Islands
islands.line: Indian Ocean reef, granite and volcanic islands, and an ecology that evolved on its own.
islands.tone_note: Forest turned toward the ocean. The only one of the five you could name blind.
